source.origin: RefSeq Complete Genomes paired to SRA short-read runs, contributed by a PlasBench collaborator and copied into the repository with their permission; every row verified again at NCBI by this selection.

criteria.rule: Start from every RefSeq Complete Genome in the contributed pool that has at least one linked SRA run.
A BioSample is used once, and never if an earlier cohort (public-v1 to v3) already holds it (cohorts/accepted_accessions.tsv).
The sequencing evidence must name a long-read platform (the rule `validate-cohort --online` enforces), so the genome can serve as long-read truth.
Short-read-first and unclassified truths are also accepted; each row carries truth_assembly_strategy, and the headline analysis uses long-read-first rows only.
When plasmids.tsv is available, its plasmid rows must agree with the assembly's own plasmid list.
Release date for the leakage arms is the earlier of the assembly release and the first read run year (read as 1 January).
Rows public on or after 2025-01-01 are labelled recent, earlier rows older (selection_arm), so recent and older genomes can be compared for database leakage.
Every passing isolate is kept: no cap per species and no one-per-study rule. cluster_key and bioproject name the study, so the analysis resamples studies, not isolates.
Each candidate is verified at NCBI: Complete Genome, plasmid replicons declared, long-read platform in the sequencing evidence, the genome's BioSample matches.

Each listed SRA run must be the same BioSample, ILLUMINA and PAIRED, and its BioProject must be one of the assembly's BioProjects (the pool's own bioproject column is the RefSeq umbrella). The row's BioProject is the run's.
Pre-download read QC from SRA run-info: estimated depth, read pairs and mean read length are graded against config/short_read_qc_thresholds.tsv. Under reject = dropped; under warn = kept and flagged.
The best passing run is chosen (pass before warn; at or under 300x deepest first, deeper runs only if nothing shallower passes); the others stay in alternate_paired_runs.
The 98 isolates of the first, balanced public-v4 selection are kept as panel_subset=core; everything else verified is panel_subset=extended.

offline.reason: No long-read platform in the sequencing evidence (cannot serve as long-read truth)
The BioSample is already in an earlier cohort (public-v1 to v3)
The BioSample appears more than once in the pool (kept once)

ncbi.reason: The SRA run's BioProject is not one of the assembly's BioProjects (not a verified pair)
Estimated read depth under the reject limit (10x)

reads.platform: Illumina, paired-end (verified at NCBI for every row)

limits: Verified at NCBI means the deposited metadata links the genome and the run; it does not prove the two come from one physical isolate beyond the BioSample.
The pre-download QC reads SRA run-info only. Base quality, adapters and pair integrity are checked after download by stage 3 (short_read_qc.py) and can still exclude a sample.

Truth strategy and polishing are derived from NCBI's assembly method and sequencing technology, not checked by a curator. Short-read-first and unclassified truths are tier 3: described, not used for the headline.
Release dates are public dates, not proof that a tool's training data or database lacks the genome; the leakage screen (LEAKAGE_* settings) compares them with each tool's database date.

Selecting every verified genome is not a designed sample: species and studies are unequal. Use cluster_key / bioproject to resample studies, and the species and panel_subset columns to choose a balanced subset.
No tool has been run on this cohort.
